literature.headline_zh: 季节性流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 我们纳入了 92,428 例 COVID-19 住院病例和 21,355 例流感住院病例。Delta 主导时期的住院率最低,而 Omicron 主导时期的 ICU 入院率最低。Omicron 时期与流感住院患者人口统计、住院时间、ICU 入院情况和住院 死亡率 最为相似。 [10.1097/ccm.0000000000007308]
在这里,我们鉴定了四种广泛识别乙型流感病毒血凝素并通过不同机制提供保护的抗体。 [10.1128/jvi.00802-26]
假病毒检测显示,K-HA 亚型导致进入某些细胞系的增加和显着的抗体逃避,这两者均归因于 A186D 突变 (A4),而流感 疫苗接种 显着增强 K 亚型的中和,表明 疫苗 具有潜在的保护作用 (A5)。 [10.1038/s41541-026-01573-y]
术前测试中,干预组有40.2%的学生知识水平较低(M ± SD = 1.68 ± 0.616);术后测试中,55.9%的学生知识水平较高(M ± SD = 1.73 ± 0.448)。在态度方面,干预后73.5%的参与者报告了积极的态度,而26.5%报告了消极的态度,这比术前测试时的60.8%消极态度有所下降。 [10.1186/s12982-026-02810-4]
所提供的证据并未明确说明直接观察到的主要结果。 [10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129118]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: We included 92,428 COVID-19 hospitalizations and 21,355 influenza hospitalizations. Hospitalization rates were lowest during the delta-dominant period, while ICU admission rates were lowest during the Omicron-dominant period. [10.1097/ccm.0000000000007308]
Here, we identified four antibodies that broadly recognize influenza B virus hemagglutinin and protect through distinct mechanisms. [10.1128/jvi.00802-26]

The pseudovirus assays showed that subclade K‐HA caused augmented entry into certain cell lines and significant antibody evasion, both of which were attributed to the A186D mutation (A4), and influenza vaccination significantly boosted neutralisation of subclade K, indicating potential vaccine protection (A5). [10.1038/s41541-026-01573-y]
At pre-test, 40.2% of the intervention group had low knowledge (M ± SD = 1.68 ± 0.616); at post-test, 55.9% had high knowledge (M ± SD = 1.73 ± 0.448). [10.1186/s12982-026-02810-4]
The supplied evidence does not clearly state a directly observed main result. [10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129118]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
我们纳入了 92,428 例 COVID-19 住院病例和 21,355 例流感住院病例。Delta 主导时期的住院率最低,而 Omicron 主导时期的 ICU 入院率最低。Omicron 时期与流感住院患者人口统计、住院时间、ICU 入院情况和住院 死亡率 最为相似。
在这里,我们鉴定了四种广泛识别乙型流感病毒血凝素并通过不同机制提供保护的抗体。 [10.1128/jvi.00802-26]。
假病毒检测显示,K-HA 亚型导致进入某些细胞系的增加和显着的抗体逃避,这两者均归因于 A186D 突变 (A4),而流感 疫苗接种 显着增强 K 亚型的中和,表明 疫苗 具有潜在的保护作用 (A5)。
术前测试中,干预组有40.2%的学生知识水平较低(M ± SD = 1.68 ± 0.616);术后测试中,55.9%的学生知识水平较高(M ± SD = 1.73 ± 0.448)。在态度方面,干预后73.5%的参与者报告了积极的态度,而26.5%报告了消极的态度,这比术前测试时的60.8%消极态度有所下降。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
We included 92,428 COVID-19 hospitalizations and 21,355 influenza hospitalizations.
Here, we identified four antibodies that broadly recognize influenza B virus hemagglutinin and protect through distinct mechanisms. [10.1128/jvi.00802-26].

The pseudovirus assays showed that subclade K‐HA caused augmented entry into certain cell lines and significant antibody evasion, both of which were attributed to the A186D mutation (A4), and influenza vaccination significantly boosted neutralisation of subclade K, indicating potential vaccine protection (A5).
At pre-test, 40.2% of the intervention group had low knowledge (M ± SD = 1.68 ± 0.616); at post-test, 55.9% had high knowledge (M ± SD = 1.73 ± 0.448). [10.1186/s12982-026-02810-4].

papers.title: Broadly reactive antibodies against influenza B virus hemagglutinin neutralize and protect through distinct structural mechanisms.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Influenza B viruses contribute substantially to seasonal disease burden; however, the structural basis by which antibodies recognize the major glycoprotein hemagglutinin (HA) and mediate antiviral activity remains incompletely defined. Influenza B virus used to circulate as two antigenically distinct lineages, B/Victoria/2/1987-like and B/Yamagata/16/1988-like, although the latter has not been detected in global surveillance in recent years. Antigenic drift in HA contributes to reduced vaccine effectiveness; however, the structural and functional basis by which antibodies recognize influenza B virus HA and mediate antiviral activity remains incompletely defined and thus thwarts our efforts in guiding next-generation vaccine design for broad protection. We characterize four murine monoclonal antibodies (mAb) that broadly bind and neutralize influenza B viruses spanning isolates across four decades of antigenic drift. Using cryo-electron microscopy coupled with in vitro and in vivo functional assays, we show that these antibodies target distinct regions of HA and confer antiviral activity through multiple mechanisms. One antibody engages the receptor-binding site and potently inhibits hemagglutination, whereas others interfere with viral egress and inhibit neuraminidase (NA) activity, suggesting steric occlusion of NA. A medial-junction antibody additionally induces antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity in vitro . Despite these mechanistic differences, all antibodies confer complete protection in mice when administered prophylactically or therapeutically. Together, these findings define distinct modes of antibody recognition of influenza B virus HA and link epitope specificity to antiviral function, providing a mechanistic understanding of correlates of immune protection and informing efforts to elicit broadly protective antibody responses against influenza B viruses. IMPORTANCE Influenza B viruses cause substantial seasonal illness, particularly in children; however, antibody responses against influenza B virus remain less well understood than those against influenza A virus. Here, we identified four antibodies that broadly recognize influenza B virus hemagglutinin and protect through distinct mechanisms. We determined cryo-electron microscopy structures of three antibody-hemagglutinin complexes to define their epitopes and explain their molecular mechanisms of action. One antibody blocks viral attachment by engaging the receptor-binding site, whereas antibodies targeting the medial junction act through post-entry antiviral activity, neuraminidase inhibition, or immune effector functions. Although the antibodies differed in neutralizing potency, all protected mice when administered before infection, and several remained effective after infection. These findings show that broad protection against influenza B virus can arise through multiple antibody targets and mechanisms, informing the evaluation and design of future vaccines and antibody-based therapies.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 流感B病毒对季节性疾病负担有显著贡献;然而,抗体如何识别主要糖蛋白血凝素(HA)并介导抗病毒药物活性的结构基础仍不完全明确。流感B病毒过去曾分为两个抗原不同的谱系,即B/Victoria/2/1987样和B/Yamagata/16/1988样,但后者近年来在全球监测中未被检测到。HA中的抗原漂移会导致疫苗效果减弱;然而,抗体如何识别流感B病毒HA并介导抗病毒药物活性的结构和功能基础仍不完全明确,从而阻碍了我们指导下一代疫苗设计以实现广泛保护的努力。我们表征了四种广谱结合并中和流感B病毒的鼠单克隆抗体(mAb),这些抗体能够中和跨越四个十年的抗原漂移分离株。通过结合冷冻电镜与体外和体内功能实验,我们发现这些抗体靶向HA的不同区域,并通过多种机制赋予抗病毒药物活性。一种抗体结合受体结合位点并强力抑制血凝,而其他抗体则干扰病毒释放并抑制神经氨酸酶(NA)活性,表明NA被空间阻断。一种中段连接区抗体在体外还诱导抗体依赖性细胞毒性。尽管这些机制存在差异,当这些抗体在预防性或治疗性给药时,均能完全保护小鼠。综上所述,这些发现定义了抗体对流感B病毒HA的不同识别模式,并将表位特异性与抗病毒药物功能联系起来,提供了免疫保护相关性的机制理解,并为诱导针对流感B病毒的广谱保护性抗体反应提供了指导。重要性 流感B病毒导致显著的季节性疾病,尤其是在儿童中;然而,针对流感B病毒的抗体反应仍不如针对流感A病毒的抗体反应那样被充分理解。在这里,我们鉴定了四种能够广谱识别流感B病毒血凝素并通过不同机制提供保护的抗体。我们确定了三种抗体-血凝素复合物的冷冻电镜结构,以定义其表位并解释其分子作用机制。一种抗体通过结合受体结合位点阻断病毒附着,而靶向中段连接区的抗体则通过进入后的抗病毒药物活性、神经氨酸酶抑制或免疫效应功能起作用。尽管这些抗体在中和效力上存在差异,但当在感染前给药时,均能保护小鼠,且其中一些在感染后仍保持有效性。这些发现表明,针对流感B病毒的广谱保护可以通过多种抗体靶点和机制实现,为未来疫苗和抗体疗法的评估与设计提供了指导。

papers.title: Host cell entry and neutralisation sensitivity of H3N2 influenza A virus subclade K.
papers.abstract: In 2025, a mutated H3N2 lineage, subclade K, emerged, showing high activity in many regions. Mutations in the hemagglutinin (HA) may affect cell entry and antibody-mediated neutralisation. Using pseudovirus particles, we show that subclade K-HA drives augmented entry into certain cell lines and displays significant antibody evasion. Both phenotypes were linked to mutation A186D. Influenza vaccination significantly boosted H3N2 subclade K neutralisation, suggesting that current vaccines may provide considerable protection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The emergence of a mutated H3N2 subclade K in 2025 raised concerns about its heightened regional activity, and it was unclear how hemagglutinin mutations might alter viral entry and antibody‐mediated neutralisation, prompting the study to investigate these properties.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was performed using pseudovirus particle assays to evaluate entry and neutralisation of subclade K‐HA, but the supplied evidence does not specify the study dates, centres, sample size, or participant composition.
analysis.methods: Using pseudovirus particles, the investigators quantified entry and neutralisation of subclade K‐HA (A3).
analysis.main_results: The pseudovirus assays showed that subclade K‐HA caused augmented entry into certain cell lines and significant antibody evasion, both of which were attributed to the A186D mutation (A4), and influenza vaccination significantly boosted neutralisation of subclade K, indicating potential vaccine protection (A5).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that despite increased entry and antibody evasion, current influenza vaccines maintain strong neutralisation against subclade K, suggesting that existing vaccination strategies remain protective.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results imply that existing H3N2 vaccines are likely to provide considerable protection against subclade K, supporting continued vaccination programs and highlighting the need for surveillance of HA mutations that affect entry and neutralisation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report any design limitations, bias, sample size constraints, or generalisability issues, and the direct experimental demonstration of entry and neutralisation effects yields a moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: An emergent H3N2 subclade K appeared in 2025 with heightened regional activity, raising questions about how hemagglutinin mutations influence viral entry and antibody neutralisation. Using pseudovirus particle assays, researchers demonstrated that subclade K‐HA enhances entry into specific cell lines and evades antibodies, both linked to the A186D mutation, while influenza vaccination markedly increased neutralisation, indicating that current vaccines remain protective. These findings suggest that existing H3N2 vaccines are likely to confer substantial protection against subclade K, supporting ongoing vaccination programs and underscoring the importance of monitoring HA mutations that affect entry and immune evasion. The study provides direct experimental evidence of entry augmentation and antibody escape, yet lacks detailed reporting of study dates, centres, sample size, and control groups, limiting full assessment of its design and generalisability; consequently, the evidence is judged moderate in strength.

papers.title: Predictors of Critical Illness During Different COVID-19 Pandemic Periods Compared With Seasonal Influenza
papers.abstract: Objectives: Since the onset of the COVID-19-pandemic, emerging virus variants, increasing population immunity, and evolving treatment strategies have substantially altered disease severity. This study aimed to identify predictors of critical illness due to COVID-19 over time and compare them with those of seasonal influenza in Sweden. Design, Setting, Patients, and Measurements: We conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study using nationwide registry data. All individuals hospitalized for COVID-19 between 2020 and 2022 were categorized into five groups, based on pandemic waves and dominating virus variants. A sixth group included all patients hospitalized for influenza between 2018 and 2022. Patients were followed from hospitalization until ICU admission, in-hospital death, discharge, or end of study. Incidence rates were calculated and Cox regression identified predictors of ICU admission and in-hospital mortality, adjusting for age, sex, socioeconomic factors, comorbidities, and severe acute respiratory syndrome corona virus 2-vaccination. Data on influenza vaccinations were not available from the registers. Main Results: We included 92,428 COVID-19 hospitalizations and 21,355 influenza hospitalizations. Hospitalization rates were lowest during the delta-dominant period, while ICU admission rates were lowest during the Omicron-dominant period. The Omicron period most closely resembled influenza inpatient demographics, hospital stay duration, ICU admissions, and in-hospital mortality. Age distributions varied across pandemic periods, with the Omicron period showing an age profile similar to influenza (≈ 50% ≥ 75 yr). Adjusted hazard ratios for ICU-admission were strongest in unvaccinated patients, males, and individuals of 45–74 years for COVID-19, and in individuals of 45–64 years or with chronic lung diseases for influenza. Common predictors of in-hospital mortality included age older than 45 years (with a sharp increase after 74), male sex, and chronic comorbidities, and for COVID-19 also unvaccinated status. Conclusions: Although COVID-19 consistently resulted in higher hospitalization rates than influenza, demographic and clinical patterns converged during the later pandemic stages. Advanced age was the strongest predictor of severe illness in both infections, with lack of vaccination additionally associated with severe COVID-19.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 自 COVID-19 大流行爆发以来,不断出现的病毒变种、人群免疫力的增强以及不断发展的 治疗 策略已大大改变了疾病的严重程度。本研究旨在确定一段时间内因 COVID-19 导致的危重疾病的预测因素,并将其与瑞典的 季节性流感 的预测因素进行比较。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们使用全国登记数据进行了一项回顾性、基于人群的 队列研究 研究。根据大流行浪潮和主要病毒变种,2020 年至 2022 年间所有因 COVID-19 住院的个人被分为五组。第六组包括 2018 年至 2022 年期间因流感住院的所有患者。
elements_zh.methods: 计算了 发病率 率,Cox 回归确定了 ICU 入院和住院 发病率 的预测因子,调整了年龄、性别、社会经济因素、合并症和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2-疫苗接种。
elements_zh.main_results: 我们纳入了 92,428 例 COVID-19 住院病例和 21,355 例流感住院病例。Delta 主导时期的住院率最低,而 Omicron 主导时期的 ICU 入院率最低。Omicron 时期与流感住院患者人口统计、住院时间、ICU 入院情况和住院 死亡率 最为相似。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管 COVID-19 的住院率始终高于流感,但人口和临床模式在大流行后期阶段趋于一致。该研究强调了疾病严重程度随时间的变化以及两种感染之间模式的趋同。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为 监测 和 季节性流感 以及 COVID-19 大流行后期阶段的风险评估策略提供信息。他们还提出了 疫苗接种 在减轻这两种感染的严重后果方面的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对登记数据的依赖而受到限制,这些数据可能缺少有关流感 疫苗接种 的信息。证据是中等的,因为研究结果基于观察数据并针对已知的混杂因素进行了调整。

papers.abstract_zh: 目标:自 COVID-19 大流行爆发以来,不断出现的病毒变种、人群免疫力的增强以及不断发展的 治疗 策略已大大改变了疾病的严重程度。本研究旨在确定一段时间内因 COVID-19 导致的危重疾病的预测因素,并将其与瑞典的 季节性流感 的预测因素进行比较。设计、设置、患者和测量:我们利用全国注册数据进行了一项回顾性、基于人群的 队列研究 研究。根据大流行浪潮和主要病毒变种,2020 年至 2022 年间所有因 COVID-19 住院的个人被分为五组。第六组包括 2018 年至 2022 年间因流感住院的所有患者。对患者从住院到入住 ICU、院内死亡、出院或研究结束进行随访。计算了 发病率 率,Cox 回归确定了 ICU 入院和住院 发病率 的预测因子,调整了年龄、性别、社会经济因素、合并症和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2-疫苗接种。登记册中未提供有关流感 疫苗接种 的数据。主要结果:我们纳入了 92,428 例 COVID-19 住院患者和 21,355 例流感住院患者。Delta 主导时期的住院率最低,而 Omicron 主导时期的 ICU 入院率最低。Omicron 时期与流感住院患者人口统计、住院时间、ICU 入院情况和住院 死亡率 最为相似。不同大流行时期的年龄分布各不相同,Omicron 时期的年龄分布与流感相似(约 50% ≥ 75 岁)。在未接种疫苗的患者、男性和 45-74 岁的 COVID-19 患者中,以及在 45-64 岁或患有流感慢性肺部疾病的个体中,入住 ICU 的调整后风险比最强。院内 死亡率 的常见预测因素包括年龄超过 45 岁(74 岁以后急剧增加)、男性和慢性合并症,以及 COVID-19 的未接种疫苗状态。结论:尽管 COVID-19 的住院率始终高于流感,但在大流行后期阶段,人口统计和临床模式趋于一致。在这两种感染中,高龄是严重疾病的最强预测因素,缺乏 疫苗接种 还与严重的 COVID-19 相关。

papers.title: Immunogenicity and safety of seasonal influenza vaccine co-administered with other vaccines: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Seasonal influenza remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, highlighting the need for vaccination strategies that improve coverage and streamline vaccine delivery. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials for randomised controlled trials (RCTs), cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies, evaluating immunogenicity and safety of same-day co-administration of influenza vaccines with COVID-19 or other vaccines, compared with non-concomitant administration. Comparators included sequential administration, single vaccine administration or placebo-controlled delayed vaccination. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias tool for Randomized Trials and Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions; certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Immunogenicity was assessed using geometric mean fold rise (GMFR) in antibody titres and seroprotection rate. Safety was assessed by adverse event (AE) incidence. 52 eligible studies were included. Influenza immunogenicity was comparable between the co-administration and non-concomitant comparator group across all strains (H1N1 GMFR ratio of means (ROM): 1.02 [95% CI: 0.95–1.10]; H3N2, 1.05 [95% CI: 0.97–1.13]; B strain, 1.01 [95% CI: 0.97–1.05]). Pooled risk ratio (RR) for seroprotection was 1.00 for all three strains with 95% CIs ranging from 0.99–1.01. GMFR for COVID-19 vaccines was modestly reduced under co-administration (ROM 0.84 [95% CI: 0.74–0.95]; p = 0.006). Serious AEs were more frequent in the co-administration group compared to the non-concomitant group (RR 1.41 [95% CI: 1.07–1.86]; p = 0.014; absolute risk difference: 1.56 percentage points). Overall, co-administration preserves influenza immunogenicity but modestly reduces COVID-19 vaccine GMFR. Although safety findings warrant cautious interpretation, the low absolute risk difference supports its feasibility as a strategy to streamline vaccination schedules and improve uptake.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of co-administering seasonal influenza vaccines with other vaccines, such as COVID-19 vaccines. The study included 52 eligible studies comparing same-day co-administration with non-concomitant administration. Immunogenicity was assessed using geometric mean fold rise (GMFR) and seroprotection rates, while safety was evaluated through adverse event (AE) incidence. Results showed that influenza immunogenicity was comparable between co-administration and non-concomitant groups across all strains, with pooled risk ratios for seroprotection close to 1.00. papers.title_zh: 季节性流感 疫苗 与其他 疫苗 联合给药的免疫原性和安全性:系统评价和荟萃分析
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Seasonal influenza remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, highlighting the need for vaccination strategies that improve coverage and streamline vaccine delivery. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials for randomised controlled trials (RCTs), cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies, evaluating immunogenicity and safety of same-day co-administration of influenza vaccines with COVID-19 or other vaccines, compared with non-concomitant administration. Comparators included sequential administration, single vaccine administration or placebo-controlled delayed vaccination. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias tool for Randomized Trials and Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions; certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Immunogenicity was assessed using geometric mean fold rise (GMFR) in antibody titres and seroprotection rate. Safety was assessed by adverse event (AE) incidence. 52 eligible studies were included. Influenza immunogenicity was comparable between the co-administration and non-concomitant comparator group across all strains (H1N1 GMFR ratio of means (ROM): 1.02 [95% CI: 0.95–1.10]; H3N2, 1.05 [95% CI: 0.97–1.13]; B strain, 1.01 [95% CI: 0.97–1.05]). Pooled risk ratio (RR) for seroprotection was 1.00 for all three strains with 95% CIs ranging from 0.99–1.01. GMFR for COVID-19 vaccines was modestly reduced under co-administration (ROM 0.84 [95% CI: 0.74–0.95]; p = 0.006). Serious AEs were more frequent in the co-administration group compared to the non-concomitant group (RR 1.41 [95% CI: 1.07–1.86]; p = 0.014; absolute risk difference: 1.56 percentage points). Overall, co-administration preserves influenza immunogenicity but modestly reduces COVID-19 vaccine GMFR. Although safety findings warrant cautious interpretation, the low absolute risk difference supports its feasibility as a strategy to streamline vaccination schedules and improve uptake.

papers.title: Investments in seasonal influenza vaccination programs pack a punch for pandemic preparedness.
papers.abstract: Low- and middle-income countries with seasonal influenza immunization programs, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic were able to deliver vaccines faster and achieve, higher coverage compared to countries without such capabilities. Middle Income, (lower- and upper-) countries participating in the Partnership for International Vaccine, Initiatives (PIVI) described influenza processes and systems that contributed to more, efficient and effective COVID-19 mass vaccination campaigns because of existing, capacities. Some routine systems were easy to pivot while others required, modifications to address the need for speed and volume when responding to the, COVID-19 pandemic. While annual influenza programs are a natural "warm base" (i.e., keeping operations such as staffing and supply chains operating at a minimum sustainable level during non-crisis periods) for honing emergency response readiness in vaccination, investments in areas more specific to pandemic preparedness remain a need. Regional variations in readiness and opportunities for cooperation should also be explored.

papers.title: HA1-T138A and HA1-Q226L substitutions in H3N2 canine influenza virus contribute to binding to human-type α2,6-linked sialic acid receptors.
papers.abstract: The H3N2 canine influenza A virus (IAV), which originated from an H3N2 avian IAV, has caused outbreaks in North America and Asia. Although H3N2 canine IAV has not been reported to transmit to humans, understanding the molecular basis of receptor tropism changes is important for viral surveillance and zoonotic risk assessment. For avian-like IAVs to spill over into humans, the hemagglutinin (HA) glycoprotein on the viral surface must acquire mutations that enable binding to α2,6-linked sialic acids (SA), the primary receptors for human influenza viruses. Although H3N2 canine IAV preferentially binds to α2,3-linked SA, the primary receptors for avian viruses, repeated mutations during viral replication in dogs may lead to HA substitutions that confer binding affinity to α2,6-linked SA. In this study, we serially passaged conditionally replicating H3N2 canine IAV in α2,3-linked SA-knockout MDCK cells, which predominantly express α2,6-linked SA (human-type cells), to identify mutations in the receptor-binding domain. We then generated recombinant viruses carrying individual mutations using reverse genetics and evaluated their growth properties in human-type cells. The HA1-T138A and HA1-Q226L substitutions significantly enhanced viral replication in these cells. Furthermore, a solid-phase glycan-binding assay demonstrated that these mutations increased binding to α2,6-linked SA to levels comparable to those observed for α2,3-linked SA. Together, these findings indicate that H3N2 canine IAV has the potential to acquire mutations that enable efficient binding to α2,6-linked SA. This study suggests that the HA1-T138A and HA1-Q226L substitutions may play critical roles in the adaptation of H3N2 canine IAV to cells expressing human-type receptors.

papers.title: Secretory expression of tetrameric neuraminidase enhanced by signal peptide optimization elicits robust immunity against influenza infection in mice
papers.abstract: Neuraminidase (NA), a key surface glycoprotein of influenza viruses, represents a more conserved antigenic target than hemagglutinin (HA) and has attracted interest as a potential target for vaccines with broader protective capacity. Nevertheless, the inefficient secretory production of tetrameric NA that maintain tetramer-like structural features remains challenging.Here, we developed an optimized signal peptide, opt-sp, by introducing valine and asparagine residues at the N-terminus of the Gaussia luciferase signal peptide (Gluc-sp) and incorporating a measles virus phosphoprotein-derived tetramerization domain. In a systematic comparison with three commonly used signal peptides, including tissue plasminogen activator (tPA), immunoglobulin G signal peptide (IgG-sp), and Gluc-sp, opt-sp was associated with increased relative secretion of NA protein under the tested expression conditions. Native PAGE analysis further suggested the presence of tetramer-like NA species. In mice,a DNA vaccine encoding opt-sp-fused NA elicited substantially stronger NA-specific humoral and cellular immune responses than constructs bearing conventional signal peptides and provided improved protection against homologous A/California/04/2009 (H1N1) challenge. These findings identify opt-sp as a promising signal peptide candidate for improving recombinant NA secretion and support further evaluation of this strategy for NA-based influenza vaccine development, including future studies of heterologous protection.

papers.title_zh: 通过信号肽优化增强四聚体神经氨酸酶的分泌表达,在小鼠中引发针对流感感染的强大免疫力
papers.source_body_en: Neuraminidase (NA), a key surface glycoprotein of influenza viruses, represents a more conserved antigenic target than hemagglutinin (HA) and has attracted interest as a potential target for vaccines with broader protective capacity. Nevertheless, the inefficient secretory production of tetrameric NA that maintain tetramer-like structural features remains challenging.Here, we developed an optimized signal peptide, opt-sp, by introducing valine and asparagine residues at the N-terminus of the Gaussia luciferase signal peptide (Gluc-sp) and incorporating a measles virus phosphoprotein-derived tetramerization domain. In a systematic comparison with three commonly used signal peptides, including tissue plasminogen activator (tPA), immunoglobulin G signal peptide (IgG-sp), and Gluc-sp, opt-sp was associated with increased relative secretion of NA protein under the tested expression conditions. Native PAGE analysis further suggested the presence of tetramer-like NA species. In mice,a DNA vaccine encoding opt-sp-fused NA elicited substantially stronger NA-specific humoral and cellular immune responses than constructs bearing conventional signal peptides and provided improved protection against homologous A/California/04/2009 (H1N1) challenge. These findings identify opt-sp as a promising signal peptide candidate for improving recombinant NA secretion and support further evaluation of this strategy for NA-based influenza vaccine development, including future studies of heterologous protection.
papers.abstract_zh: 神经氨酸酶 (NA) 是流感病毒的一种关键表面糖蛋白,代表比血凝素 (HA) 更保守的抗原靶点,作为具有更广泛保护能力的 疫苗 的潜在靶点引起了人们的兴趣。然而,保持四聚体样结构特征的四聚体NA的低效分泌生产仍然具有挑战性。在这里,我们通过在高斯荧光素酶信号肽(Gluc-sp)的N末端引入缬氨酸和天冬酰胺残基并整合麻疹病毒磷蛋白衍生的四聚化结构域,开发了一种优化的信号肽opt-sp。在与三种常用信号肽(包括组织纤溶酶原激活剂 (tPA)、免疫球蛋白 G 信号肽 (IgG-sp) 和 Gluc-sp)的系统比较中,opt-sp 在测试的表达条件下与 NA 蛋白的相对分泌增加相关。天然 PAGE 分析进一步表明存在四聚体样 NA 物种。在小鼠中,编码 opt-sp 融合 NA 的 DNA 疫苗 比带有传统信号肽的构建体引发了更强的 NA 特异性体液和细胞 免疫应答,并提供了针对同源 A/California/04/2009 (H1N1) 攻击的改进保护。这些发现将 opt-sp 确定为改善重组 NA 分泌的有前途的信号肽候选者,并支持进一步评估这种基于 NA 的流感 疫苗 开发策略,包括异源保护的未来研究。

papers.title: Summary of the National Advisory Committee on Immunization (NACI) Seasonal Influenza Vaccine Statement for 2026–2027
papers.abstract: Background: The National Advisory Committee on Immunization (NACI) reviews evolving evidence on influenza immunization annually and updates vaccine recommendations.The NACI Statement on seasonal influenza vaccines for 2026-2027 updates recommendations from the 2025-2026 season.Objective: To highlight new and updated information since the 2025-2026 statement and to summarize the 2026-2027 NACI seasonal influenza vaccine recommendations.Methods: The NACI Influenza Working Group applied the NACI evidence-based process to assess available evidence and formulate recommendations, which were evaluated and approved by NACI.Throughout the process, NACI's peer-reviewed Ethics, Equity, Feasibility, and Acceptability (EEFA) framework , along with its evidence-informed tools (Ethics Integrated Filters, Equity Matrix, Feasibility Matrix, and Acceptability Matrix) were applied.Results: The overarching recommendation for seasonal influenza vaccination remains unchanged.Key updates for the 2025-2026 statement include: 1) integration of a new evidence review on optimal timing of seasonal influenza vaccination, including consideration of intraseasonal waning, and 2) integration of guidance on seasonal influenza vaccination in the context of avian influenza, with supporting resources.Conclusion: This guidance reaffirms NACI's recommendation that influenza vaccine should be offered annually to anyone six months of age or older who does not have a contraindication to the vaccine.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review outlines NACI’s annual assessment of influenza immunization and states its objective to present updates and summarize the 2026‐2027 seasonal influenza vaccine recommendations for the general population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The NACI Influenza Working Group employed the NACI evidence‐based process, incorporating the EEFA framework and associated equity, feasibility and acceptability matrices, to evaluate the evidence and formulate the recommendations.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The statement concludes that the overall recommendation for seasonal influenza vaccination remains unchanged, reaffirming that vaccination should be offered annually to all individuals aged six months and older without contraindications.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The authors note that new evidence on the optimal timing of vaccination, including intraseasonal waning, and guidance for vaccination amid avian influenza, indicates remaining uncertainties about timing and cross‐virus interactions.

analysis.summary_en: The NACI seasonal influenza vaccine statement for 2026‐2027 reviews annual evidence, updates recommendations, and reaffirms the unchanged guidance that all individuals six months or older should receive influenza vaccination annually if not contraindicated. The Working Group applied NACI’s evidence‐based process with the EEFA framework and related matrices to assess data. While the core recommendation stays stable, the document identifies gaps in knowledge about optimal vaccination timing, intraseasonal waning, and the influence of avian influenza, signalling areas for future study. Consequently, the guidance emphasizes continued annual vaccination and calls for research to refine timing strategies and address interactions with avian influenza strains.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:国家免疫咨询委员会(NACI)每年审查流感疫苗接种的最新证据,并更新疫苗建议。2026-2027年度NACI关于季节性流感 疫苗的声明更新了2025-2026年度的建议。目标:强调自2025-2026年度声明以来的新信息和更新内容,并总结2026-2027年度NACI关于季节性流感 疫苗的建议。方法:NACI流感工作组应用了NACI的循证流程,评估现有证据并制定建议,这些建议经NACI评估和批准。在整个过程中,应用了NACI的同行评审伦理、公平性、可行性和可接受性(EEFA)框架,以及相关的伦理整合筛选工具、公平性矩阵、可行性矩阵和可接受性矩阵。结果:对于季节性流感 疫苗接种的整体建议保持不变。2025-2026年度声明的关键更新包括:1)整合了关于季节性流感 疫苗接种最佳接种时机的新证据审查,包括对季节内免疫力减弱的考虑;2)整合了在禽流感背景下接种季节性流感 疫苗接种的指导,并提供了支持资源。结论:该指导重申了NACI的建议,即流感疫苗应每年提供给任何六岁及以上且无接种禁忌症的个体。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查概述了NACI对流感疫苗接种的年度评估,并说明其目标是提供更新信息并总结2026-2027年度针对一般人群的季节性流感 疫苗建议。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: NACI流感工作组采用了NACI的循证流程,结合EEFA框架及相关公平性、可行性和可接受性矩阵,以评估证据并制定建议。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 声明得出结论,对于季节性流感 疫苗接种的整体建议保持不变,重申应每年为所有六岁及以上且无禁忌症的个体提供疫苗接种。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 作者指出,关于疫苗接种最佳接种时机的新证据,包括季节内免疫力减弱,以及在禽流感背景下接种疫苗接种的指导,表明对接种时机和跨病毒相互作用仍存在不确定性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 实际上,该指南建议符合条件的人员继续进行年度 疫苗,并强调需要进一步研究 疫苗 时机以及禽流感对季节性 疫苗 策略的影响。

papers.title: Linear DNA expression cassette encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles confers complete protection against influenza A virus in mice
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT DNA-based vaccines have been developed and tested against a range of infectious agents, including influenza A viruses (IAV). Bacterial plasmid DNA is widely used as a vector for delivering genes encoding vaccine immunogens. However, the inclusion of antibiotic resistance genes in conventional plasmid constructs raises safety concerns. Linear DNA expression cassettes produced via PCR that lack antibiotic resistance genes, and bacterial sequences can serve as a safer alternative vector. In this study, we employed a mouse model of IAV to evaluate the protective efficacy of a lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated linear DNA expression cassette containing the hemagglutinin gene of IAV H1N1 produced by PCR amplification. For comparison, a circular plasmid DNA containing the same gene was also constructed. The LNP-encapsulated DNA cassette (LNP-L) exhibited similar physicochemical characteristics, such as particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, and encapsulation efficiency, compared to the LNP-encapsulated circular plasmid DNA (LNP-P). However, LNP-L produced significantly lower transgene expression than LNP-P in cell culture. Mice immunized with LNP-L developed a delayed onset of antibody response compared to those immunized with LNP-P, but the magnitudes of both humoral and cell-mediated immune responses were comparable between the two groups after booster immunization. Moreover, mice immunized with LNP-L exhibited both Th1 and Th2 responses, similar to those immunized with LNP-P. Importantly, mice immunized with either LNP-L or LNP-P were fully protected upon challenge with a lethal dose of IAV H1N1. These findings suggest that linear DNA expression cassettes encapsulated in LNPs represent a promising strategy for vaccine development. IMPORTANCE Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated DNA vaccines represent a promising platform for the rapid development of vaccines against infectious pathogens. However, the inclusion of an antibiotic-resistance gene in plasmid DNA vectors used to deliver vaccine immunogens raises potential safety concerns. This study explores the feasibility of using a linear expression cassette produced via PCR amplification as an alternative system for delivering vaccine immunogens. Compared with conventional plasmid DNA, the linear expression cassette contains only essential elements, including a promoter, the gene encoding the vaccine immunogen, and a polyadenylation signal, and can be produced in a cell-free system. Using a mouse model for influenza A virus, we demonstrate that an LNP-encapsulated linear DNA cassette induces humoral and cell-mediated immune responses and protects immunized mice against a lethal influenza virus challenge. Thus, the LNP-encapsulated linear expression cassette may provide a safer approach for rapid responses to infectious diseases in animals.

papers.title_original: Linear DNA expression cassette encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles confers complete protection against influenza A virus in mice

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate a safer DNA vaccine strategy for influenza A virus by using a linear DNA expression cassette instead of conventional plasmid DNA vectors, which include antibiotic resistance genes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a mouse model of influenza A virus to assess the protective efficacy of a lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated linear DNA expression cassette containing the hemagglutinin gene of IAV H1N1.
analysis.methods: Linear DNA expression cassettes were produced via PCR amplification without antibiotic resistance genes, and were encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles. A circular plasmid DNA containing the same gene was also constructed for comparison. The protective efficacy was tested by challenging mice with a lethal dose of IAV H1N1.
analysis.main_results: The LNP-encapsulated linear DNA cassette (LNP-L) showed similar physicochemical properties to the LNP-encapsulated circular plasmid DNA (LNP-P). Mice immunized with LNP-L had a delayed onset of antibody response but comparable humoral and cell-mediated immune responses after booster immunization. Both LNP-L and LNP-P fully protected mice against a lethal influenza virus challenge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that linear DNA expression cassettes encapsulated in LNPs could be a promising strategy for vaccine development, as they offer a safer alternative without compromising protective efficacy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results indicate that this approach may provide a safer and more efficient method for rapid vaccine development against seasonal influenza viruses in animals, with potential implications for human vaccine design.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a mouse model and does not address human immune responses or long-term safety, but the evidence is strong as it directly compares the efficacy of linear and circular DNA vectors in a relevant animal model.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the use of a linear DNA expression cassette encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles (LNP) as a safer alternative to conventional plasmid DNA vectors for influenza A virus (IAV) vaccination. The research focuses on the protective efficacy of the LNP-encapsulated linear DNA cassette (LNP-L) in a mouse model of IAV H1N1. The evidence is strong due to direct comparison in a relevant animal model.

papers.title_zh: 封装在脂质纳米粒子中的线性 DNA 表达盒为小鼠提供针对甲型流感病毒的完全保护
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT DNA-based vaccines have been developed and tested against a range of infectious agents, including influenza A viruses (IAV). Bacterial plasmid DNA is widely used as a vector for delivering genes encoding vaccine immunogens. However, the inclusion of antibiotic resistance genes in conventional plasmid constructs raises safety concerns. Linear DNA expression cassettes produced via PCR that lack antibiotic resistance genes, and bacterial sequences can serve as a safer alternative vector. In this study, we employed a mouse model of IAV to evaluate the protective efficacy of a lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated linear DNA expression cassette containing the hemagglutinin gene of IAV H1N1 produced by PCR amplification. For comparison, a circular plasmid DNA containing the same gene was also constructed. The LNP-encapsulated DNA cassette (LNP-L) exhibited similar physicochemical characteristics, such as particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, and encapsulation efficiency, compared to the LNP-encapsulated circular plasmid DNA (LNP-P). However, LNP-L produced significantly lower transgene expression than LNP-P in cell culture. Mice immunized with LNP-L developed a delayed onset of antibody response compared to those immunized with LNP-P, but the magnitudes of both humoral and cell-mediated immune responses were comparable between the two groups after booster immunization. Moreover, mice immunized with LNP-L exhibited both Th1 and Th2 responses, similar to those immunized with LNP-P. Importantly, mice immunized with either LNP-L or LNP-P were fully protected upon challenge with a lethal dose of IAV H1N1. These findings suggest that linear DNA expression cassettes encapsulated in LNPs represent a promising strategy for vaccine development. IMPORTANCE Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated DNA vaccines represent a promising platform for the rapid development of vaccines against infectious pathogens. However, the inclusion of an antibiotic-resistance gene in plasmid DNA vectors used to deliver vaccine immunogens raises potential safety concerns. This study explores the feasibility of using a linear expression cassette produced via PCR amplification as an alternative system for delivering vaccine immunogens. Compared with conventional plasmid DNA, the linear expression cassette contains only essential elements, including a promoter, the gene encoding the vaccine immunogen, and a polyadenylation signal, and can be produced in a cell-free system. Using a mouse model for influenza A virus, we demonstrate that an LNP-encapsulated linear DNA cassette induces humoral and cell-mediated immune responses and protects immunized mice against a lethal influenza virus challenge. Thus, the LNP-encapsulated linear expression cassette may provide a safer approach for rapid responses to infectious diseases in animals.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 基于 DNA 的 疫苗 已针对一系列感染原进行了开发和测试,包括甲型流感病毒 (IAV)。细菌质粒 DNA 被广泛用作 媒介,用于传递编码 疫苗 免疫原的基因。然而,传统质粒构建体中包含抗生素抗性基因引起了安全问题。通过 PCR 产生的缺乏抗生素抗性基因的线性 DNA 表达盒和细菌序列可以作为更安全的替代品 媒介。在本研究中,我们采用 IAV 小鼠模型来评估脂质纳米颗粒 (LNP) 封装的线性 DNA 表达盒的保护功效,该表达盒含有通过 PCR 扩增产生的 IAV H1N1 血凝素基因。为了进行比较,还构建了含有相同基因的环状质粒DNA。与 LNP 封装的环状质粒 DNA (LNP-P) 相比,LNP 封装的 DNA 盒 (LNP-L) 表现出相似的物理化学特性,例如粒径、多分散指数、zeta 电位和封装效率。然而,在细胞培养中,LNP-L 产生的转基因表达显着低于 LNP-P。与用 LNP-P 免疫的小鼠相比,用 LNP-L 免疫的小鼠出现了延迟的抗体反应,但在加强免疫后,两组之间体液和细胞介导的 免疫应答 的强度相当。此外,用 LNP-L 免疫的小鼠表现出 Th1 和 Th2 反应,与用 LNP-P 免疫的小鼠相似。重要的是,用 LNP-L 或 LNP-P 免疫的小鼠在受到致死剂量的 IAV H1N1 攻击后得到了充分的保护。这些发现表明,封装在 LNP 中的线性 DNA 表达盒代表了 疫苗 开发的一种有前途的策略。重要性 脂质纳米颗粒 (LNP) 封装的 DNA 疫苗 代表了快速开发 疫苗 对抗传染性病原体的有前景的平台。然而,用于传递 疫苗 免疫原的质粒 DNA 媒介 中包含的抗生素抗性基因引起了潜在的安全问题。本研究探讨了使用通过 PCR 扩增产生的线性表达盒作为传递 疫苗 免疫原的替代系统的可行性。与传统的质粒DNA相比,线性表达盒仅包含必需的元件,包括启动子、编码疫苗免疫原的基因和聚腺苷酸化信号,并且可以在无细胞系统中产生。使用甲型流感病毒小鼠模型,我们证明 LNP 封装的线性 DNA 盒可诱导体液和细胞介导的 免疫应答 并保护免疫小鼠免受致命流感病毒的攻击。因此,LNP封装的线性表达盒可以为快速应对动物传染病提供更安全的方法。

papers.title: N6-methyladenosine regulates Influenza A virus mRNA stability yet is rarely found on genomic RNA
papers.abstract: Previous studies have found widespread N6-methyladenosine (m6A methylation) on all forms of Influenza A virus (IAV) RNA, with m6A found critical for viral replication, pathogenicity as well as viral RNA packaging. Here we applied the latest quantitative technologies to revisit the methylation landscape on the anti-sense genomic RNA of IAV. Unexpectedly, upon Ultra-Performance Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) analysis of IAV virion -extracted genomic RNA, we detected very little m6A regardless of production from human cells or chicken eggs. Concordantly, Nanopore direct RNA sequencing also detected an overall low occurrence and stoichiometry (generally <5%) of m6A across all viral genomic RNA segments, compared with abundant m6A sites on viral mRNAs at ~20-30% m6A. Cross validation with glyoxal- and nitrite-mediated deamination of unmethylated adenosines (GLORI) confirmed multiple m6A sites on viral mRNA yet very few m6A on the genomic RNA. This paucity of m6A on genomic RNA makes it unlikely that m6A contributes to viral RNA packaging. Knockdown or pharmacological inhibition of the m6A methyltransferase METTL3 as well as the reader protein YTHDF2 both reduced viral mRNA levels and infectious viral particle production, with YTHDF2 promoting viral mRNA stability. Thus, the presence of m6A on IAV transcripts is indeed proviral, yet it is the mRNAs instead of genomic RNAs that are methylated at functionally relevant levels. Lastly, we provide proof of concept that a METTL3 small molecule inhibitor can be antiviral, and propose that m6A-targeted antivirals would mainly impact the intracellular gene expression phase of IAV replication.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation in Influenza A virus (IAV) RNA. Previous research suggested m6A was critical for viral replication, pathogenicity, and RNA packaging. The study revisits the methylation landscape of IAV genomic RNA using advanced quantitative methods and finds that m6A is present at very low levels on genomic RNA, regardless of production from human cells or chicken eggs. In contrast, m6A is abundant on viral mRNAs, with Nanopore sequencing showing ~20-30% m6A coverage. Cross-validation using GLORI confirmed the presence of m6A on mRNAs but not on genomic RNA. These findings suggest that m6A does not play a significant role in genomic RNA packaging but instead contributes to mRNA stability and viral replication. The study also demonstrates that targeting METTL3 with small molecule inhibitors can have antiviral effects, highlighting potential therapeutic strategies. However, the study does not explore the broader implications of these findings for public health or clinical applications.

papers.title: ATTITUDES AND PRACTICES TOWARDS COVID-19 AND SEASONAL FLU VACCINES AND VACCINATION IN THE GENERAL POPULATION AND AMONG MEDICAL PROFESSIONALS
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has led to the development of several types of vaccines, among which messenger RNA (mRNA)-based vaccines have represented a significant breakthrough. This study aimed to evaluate attitudes towards COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccination among the general population and individuals with a medical background. A questionnaire was developed to collect sociodemographic data, personal health information, vaccination status, and information on participants’ attitudes towards and knowledge of vaccines. The profile of the typical participant was an employed woman with tertiary education, living with another person in an urban area and reporting generally good health. The typical participant had received at least two doses of the Sputnik V vaccine. Participants generally expressed favourable attitudes towards regular COVID-19 vaccination. The results showed no apparent differences between participants with and without a medical background regarding vaccine choice, the decision to receive a third dose, or seasonal influenza vaccination. Similarly, no apparent differences were observed in attitudes towards the AstraZeneca vaccine or mandatory COVID-19 vaccination between respondents with and without a medical background.

papers.title_zh: 关于冠状病毒病2019年(COVID-19)和季节性流感疫苗和疫苗接种在一般人群和医疗专业人员中的态度和做法
papers.source_body_en: The COVID-19 pandemic has led to the development of several types of vaccines, among which messenger RNA (mRNA)-based vaccines have represented a significant breakthrough. This study aimed to evaluate attitudes towards COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccination among the general population and individuals with a medical background. A questionnaire was developed to collect sociodemographic data, personal health information, vaccination status, and information on participants’ attitudes towards and knowledge of vaccines. The profile of the typical participant was an employed woman with tertiary education, living with another person in an urban area and reporting generally good health. The typical participant had received at least two doses of the Sputnik V vaccine. Participants generally expressed favourable attitudes towards regular COVID-19 vaccination. The results showed no apparent differences between participants with and without a medical background regarding vaccine choice, the decision to receive a third dose, or seasonal influenza vaccination. Similarly, no apparent differences were observed in attitudes towards the AstraZeneca vaccine or mandatory COVID-19 vaccination between respondents with and without a medical background.

papers.full_text: Article summary AI generated Seasonal influenza poses significant health risks globally, making vaccination a crucial preventive measure. This study demonstrated that a structured educational intervention significantly improved university students' knowledge and attitudes towards the seasonal influenza vaccine in Iraq, leading to increased vaccination uptake. Abstract Background & aim Influenza is a serious viral respiratory disease, and vaccination is the primary means of prevention. The purpose of the present study was to evaluate the effectiveness of an intervention program in improving university students’ knowledge and attitudes regarding the seasonal influenza vaccine. Materials and methods A quasi-experimental design was employed, with convenience sampling of 204 students (102 intervention, 102 control) over a period of six months at Thi-Qar University (TQU) in southern Iraq, across six colleges selected via a simple random lottery. Students’ knowledge and attitudes were measured using a structured educational program, brochures, and pre- and post-tests. Independent- and paired-samples t-tests were used to analyze the data, with a significance level of p < 0.05. Results At pre-test, 40.2% of the intervention group had low knowledge (M ± SD = 1.68 ± 0.616); at post-test, 55.9% had high knowledge (M ± SD = 1.73 ± 0.448). In terms of attitudes, 73.5% of participants reported positive attitudes after the intervention, while 26.5% reported negative attitudes, a decrease from pre-test, where 60.8% stated that they had negative attitudes. Conclusion Significant change in knowledge and attitudes in relation to seasonal influenza vaccine following intervention (p < 0.001). A structured educational intervention is an effective strategy to increase university students’ acceptance of flu vaccines in Iraq. University-based influenza vaccination programs are recommended to improve vaccine coverage and reduce influenza-related disease. 1 Introduction Globally, influenza is a severe viral respiratory illness that significantly increases morbidity and mortality. Human illness could be caused by influenza virus types A, B, and C. Because of its high vulnerability to antigenic change, influenza A is the type most frequently responsible for pandemics [1]. The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that one billion people worldwide are affected by seasonal influenza each year, which causes between 290,000 and 650,000 influenza-associated respiratory deaths and 3–5 million episodes of severe illness [2]. Even though there are several antiviral medications that have been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and are accessible in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR), vaccination is still thought to be the most effective way to prevent influenza. These vaccinations only provide protection against the vaccine antigen, and their effectiveness diminishes with time [3, 4]. Yearly, the Centers for Disease Prevention and Control (CDC) recommends individuals that aged from six months of age and older to get the seasonal influenza vaccine. The most common kind of vaccine is an intramuscular inactivated vaccine that contains a killed virus strain [5, 6]. Influenza vaccines can prevent morbidity and mortality andlessen the spread and severity of the disease. They are safe and generally well tolerated, do not cause influenza disease, and very rarely have major adverse effects. They are also essential in lowering the health and economic burden of influenza [7, 8]. Influenza outbreaks typically happen in the final autumn and all winter months. Adults should receive a yearly injection of a single dose (0.5 cc) of an influenza vaccination, ideally by October. For best results, children ages 6 months to 8 years need to receive two doses of the influenza vaccine during their first immunization season, spaced at least 4 weeks apart [9, 10]. Globally, several intervention and survey studies have explored educational strategies to increase influenza vaccination knowledge and attitudes. Abushouk et al. 2023 reported that the targeted educational interventions had a significant effect on the knowledge and practice of health sciences university students regarding the seasonal influenza vaccine in Saudi Arabia [11]. Similarly, Walker et al. (2016) conducted a study amongst medical students in Australia, which found that knowledge and attitudes were strongly linked to vaccination uptake, highlighting the importance of structured learning in improving vaccine uptake [12]. The results of this study suggest that educational programs can be effective in addressing knowledge gaps and vaccine hesitancy across a variety of cultural contexts, supporting the rationale for the current study. To assess the effectiveness of intervention program regarding seasonal influenza vaccine among university students and to enhance vaccination coverage the present study was conducted. 2 Methods Study design: quasi- experimental design was selected to obtain the current study aims. Study period: the study period was 6 months starting from 1st September to the end of February. Data collection was done by working two days per week. The applying of intervention program was continued for 4 months. Study setting: the study was conducted at Thi-qar university, Al- Nasiryiah city, southern Iraq at 6 college out of 18 colleges at the university. The colleges were selected randomly. Study Population: The students of selected colleges of the University were recruited. 17 students from each college were chosen based on a proportional allocation to achieve a total sample of approximately 102 participants per group (17 × 6 = 102), which was determined to be sufficient based on a power analysis (power = 0.80, alpha = 0.05, medium effect size) to detect significant differences in knowledge and attitude scores. 2.1 An intervention group definition The intervention health education program involved four months of structured education through face-to-face lectures (on influenza etiology, transmission, complications and vaccine safety/efficacy); distribution of informational brochures, and interactive question and answer sessions. The intervention group consisted of university students who participated in this education program about seasonal influenza vaccine. 2.2 A control group definition The control group included 102 students (17 students from each of the same 6 colleges) matched to the intervention group by college and academic year that were not went received intervention program on seasonal influenza vaccine. Study Hypothesis: The current study hypothesis display that if there is a significant or non-significant relationship between study variables. - H0: suggest no significant association between pre and post intervention of student knowledge & attitudes regarding seasonal influenza vaccine. - H1: suggest significant association between pre and post intervention of student knowledge & attitudes regarding seasonal influenza vaccine. Study Sample: Convenience sample consisting from 204 students (102 study& 102 control) who eligible to participate and fitted the inclusion criteria. The inclusion criteria were student from different colleges and different stages, while the exclusion criteria were student who don’t complete the intervention program lectures in addition to those who got a score more than 80% at pretest. Study Tools: Pre-test was conducted on student’s introduction of constructed educational programs, brochures and questionnaire to assess students’ knowledge and attitude about seasonal influenza vaccine, then post test was conducted after implementation of intervention program to determine the impact of intervention program. The questionnaire consisted of three parts: (1) Demographic information sheet, and age, gender, residence, and academic specialization; (2) Knowledge sheet, comprising 15 items which assessed students’ knowledge about influenza disease, its complications, influenza transmission routes, and the influenza vaccine (types of vaccine, safety, efficacy, and influenza vaccine schedule); and (3) Attitude sheet, comprising 10 items which assessed students’ attitudes toward influenza vaccine, perceived necessity, and perceived safety perceptions of the influenza vaccine. Ranging and Scoring: A three-point Likert scale was used for rating all knowledge items (Yes = 2, Uncertain = 1, No = 0) and attitude items (Agree = 2, Neutral = 1, Disagree = 0) [13]. The questionnaire was adapted from validated questionnaires that were used in previous studies [14, 15] and administered in Arabic, the students’ native language. The instrument was first tested on a sample of 20 students (not in the final sample) for clarity, comprehension and timing, and slight changes were made to the instrument based on this pilot testing. A panel of five expert nurses and public health experts confirmed the content validity. The degree of knowledge and attitudes were assessed by the cutoff point and by the mean score. The mean score for each part was computed by adding up all item scores and dividing into three parts: (i) Low (< 33rd percentile), (ii) Fair (33rd–66th percentile) and (iii) High (> 66th percentile) for knowledge; and Negative (< mean) and Positive (≥ mean) for attitudes. The mean was calculated using neutral/uncertain responses given as intermediate (score = 1). Statistical analysis: SPSS version 26 was used to analyze data. The present study used descriptive and inferential statistics such as mean, standard deviation (SD), independent samples t-test and paired samples t-test. A level of p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. 3 Results Table 1 shows the descriptive results of the present study. In terms of gender, 58.8% of the intervention group were females and 41.2% were males, whereas 54.9% of the control group were female and 45.1% were male. As for age, 49.0% of those in the intervention group were in the age group of 18 to 20 years while 52.9% of those in the control group were in the age group of 21 to 25 years. In regard to place of residence, the proportion of each group who lived in urban areas (53.9% and 66.7%, respectively) was higher for both intervention and control groups. Lastly, of the student specializations, 69.6% of the intervention group and 51.0% of the control group were scientific. In the intervention group, results displayed that (40.2%) of students have a low knowledge regarding seasonal influenza vaccine at period of the pre-test with M ± SD (1.68±0.616). While at period of the post-test, findings showed that (55.9%) declared a high knowledge level with M ± SD equal to (1.73±0.448). The control group expressed 49.0% of student have a fair knowledge regarding seasonal influenza vaccine at pre and post test period with M ± SD (2.04±0.716), Table 2, 3 revealed that 60.8% of students at intervention group and 67.6% of student at control group have a negative attitude regarding seasonal influenza vaccine at pre- test period where the M ± SD was (1.39±0.491, 1.32±0.470) respectively. While at post- test period the study group demonstrated 73.5% of students have a positive attitude regarding seasonal influenza vaccine and 67.6% of students at control group have a negative attitude. The current results showed at Table 4, there was a highly statistically difference in overall assessment of student knowledge, vaccination status, family vaccination history and attitudes between two periods pre and post applying the intervention program among university students where the p- value for all variables was (< 0.001). Table 5 demonstrated that no statistical difference in students’ knowledge regarding seasonal influenza vaccine was found between intervention and control group at pre- test period (t=-1.599; p = 0.111, 95% CI: -0.328 to 0.034) while there was a highly statistical difference in students’ knowledge at post test period between two groups where (t = 6.194; p < 0.001, 95% CI: 0.408 to 0.788). In respect to students’ vaccination status at pre -test periods, no statistical association was found between intervention and control groups (t = 1.497; p = 0.136, 95% CI: -0.031 to 0.227) but at post - intervention program there was a statistically association found between both groups (t= -7.361; p = 0.000). According to students’ family vaccination status the present outcome reveal that no difference was found at pre- intervention between study and control group (t= -1.616; p = 0.108, 95% CI: -0.348 to 0.035), in contrast to the post intervention program applying there was a statistical difference in students family vaccination status between both groups (t = 7.694; p = 0.000). Finally, regarding students attitudes, no statistical differences was found at pre- intervention between intervention and control group (t = 1.020; p = 0.309, 95% CI: -0.064 to 0.201) but in other hand there was a statistical difference between both groups at post intervention program applying period (t = 6.435; p < 0.001, 95% CI: 0.286 to 0.538). 4 Discussion The purpose of the present study was to examine if an intervention program would have a positive effect on university students’ knowledge and attitude towards seasonal influenza vaccine in Thi Qar University, Iraq. The results showed the importance of the intervention program to students’ knowledge, attitudes and vaccination status. 4.1 Knowledge regarding seasonal influenza vaccine In intervention group, before intervention, 40.2% of students had low knowledge and 7.8% had high knowledge on seasonal influenza vaccine. This finding concurs with the numerous studies that have been conducted in the Middle East region previously which have consistently indicated little knowledge on influenza vaccination among university students. This comes in agreement with [9, 15, 16]. The failure to recognize influenza vaccines is a large barrier to uptake of vaccines, and is emblematic of the wider problem of limited health education programs about preventive measures to health in the university setting. After the intervention, level of knowledge improved substantially − 55.9% of students in the intervention group contrasted to 27.5% in the control group. After intervention, there is a highly significant difference (p = 0.000) between the groups in that structured educational programs are very effective in empowering students to learn about the seasonal influenza vaccines. Comparing to Abushouk et al. (2023), we report similar findings, where we determined that those educational interventions effectively increased knowledge about influenza vaccination in the university population [11]. 4.2 Attitudes towards seasonal influenza vaccine Before intervention, the attitude of both intervention (60.8%) and control (67.6%) groups towards seasonal influenza vaccine showed predominantly negative attitudes. This is consistent with the known general vaccine hesitancy seen across the Eastern Mediterranean Region [1, 17]. Misconceptions about vaccine safety, efficacy and necessity have been related to negative attitudes toward vaccines and to cultural and social factors which affect village (village, region) people’s health seeking behavior this is the approximately similar to Smith S. et al. (2016) and Abd K. et al. (2021) [18, 19]. Attitudes were remarkably changed in the intervention group post intervention − 73.5 vs. 32.4% of students in the control group had positive attitudes. This significant improvement (p < 0.001) is therefore indicative of the fact that well designed educational interventions can in fact address misconceptions and concerns surrounding the influenza vaccine. As attitudes play a strong role in predicting vaccination behavior (WHO, 2022), it is most significant that this study has observed a change in attitudes [20]. 4.3 Vaccination status An outcome of this study was improvement in the self-reported vaccination status of the students in the intervention group. This difference (p < 0.001) is highly significant in vaccination status after the intervention between the intervention and the control group’s post intervention indicates that increased knowledge and better attitudes leadto behavioral change and these results agree with Walker L et al. and Lu P et al. (2021) [12, 21]. This finding has implications as it means education does not only increase knowledge and attitude but also improve the vaccination uptake. In addition, after the intervention, there were statistically significant differences (p = 0.000) on the family vaccination status between the intervention and control groups the present results come in line with Goss MD. et al. (2020) and Sales et al. (2012) [22, 23]. This implies that the intervention could have a second wave as educated students might persuade their family to choose the better health options thus extending the influence of the intervention on the people whom they come in contact with. 4.4 Limitations and strengths This study has several limitations. The first drawback of the convenience sampling method is that it may not generalize the findings to the entire university student population. Second, the status of vaccination may be subject to recall bias or social desirability bias, as it is self-reported. The study does not include a long term follow up to explore the sustainability of the knowledge gain and of attitude change. Although these limitations exist, the study has several strengths, most importantly a quasi-experimental design with a control group, which makes it possible to have a stronger conclusion about the effectiveness of the intervention. In addition, it adds to the diversity of the sample through the inclusion of students from different colleges and specializations. 4.5 Implications for practice The findings presented in this study are of key importance for public health practice in Iraq and similar environments. They then emphasize the imperative for organized curricular programmes on seasonal influenza vaccine…

This study demonstrated that a structured educational intervention significantly improved university students' knowledge and attitudes towards the seasonal influenza vaccine in Iraq, leading to increased vaccination uptake. Abstract Background & aim Influenza is a serious viral respiratory disease, and vaccination is the primary means of prevention. The purpose of the present study was to evaluate the effectiveness of an intervention program in improving university students’ knowledge and attitudes regarding the seasonal influenza vaccine. Materials and methods A quasi-experimental design was employed, with convenience sampling of 204 students (102 intervention, 102 control) over a period of six months at Thi-Qar University (TQU) in southern Iraq, across six colleges selected via a simple random lottery. Students’ knowledge and attitudes were measured using a structured educational program, brochures, and pre- and post-tests. Independent- and paired-samples t-tests were used to analyze the data, with a significance level of p < 0.05. Results At pre-test, 40.2% of the intervention group had low knowledge (M ± SD = 1.68 ± 0.616); at post-test, 55.9% had high knowledge (M ± SD = 1.73 ± 0.448). In terms of attitudes, 73.5% of participants reported positive attitudes after the intervention, while 26.5% reported negative attitudes, a decrease from pre-test, where 60.8% stated that they had negative attitudes. Conclusion Significant change in knowledge and attitudes in relation to seasonal influenza vaccine following intervention (p < 0.001). A structured educational intervention is an effective strategy to increase university students’ acceptance of flu vaccines in Iraq. University-based influenza vaccination programs are recommended to improve vaccine coverage and reduce influenza-related disease. 1 Introduction Globally, influenza is a severe viral respiratory illness that significantly increases morbidity and mortality. Human illness could be caused by influenza virus types A, B, and C. Because of its high vulnerability to antigenic change, influenza A is the type most frequently responsible for pandemics [1]. The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that one billion people worldwide are affected by seasonal influenza each year, which causes between 290,000 and 650,000 influenza-associated respiratory deaths and 3–5 million episodes of severe illness [2]. Even though there are several antiviral medications that have been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and are accessible in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR), vaccination is still thought to be the most effective way to prevent influenza. These vaccinations only provide protection against the vaccine antigen, and their effectiveness diminishes with time [3, 4]. Yearly, the Centers for Disease Prevention and Control (CDC) recommends individuals that aged from six months of age and older to get the seasonal influenza vaccine. The most common kind of vaccine is an intramuscular inactivated vaccine that contains a killed virus strain [5, 6]. Influenza vaccines can prevent morbidity and mortality andlessen the spread and severity of the disease. They are safe and generally well tolerated, do not cause influenza disease, and very rarely have major adverse effects. They are also essential in lowering the health and economic burden of influenza [7, 8]. Influenza outbreaks typically happen in the final autumn and all winter months. Adults should receive a yearly injection of a single dose (0.5 cc) of an influenza vaccination, ideally by October. For best results, children ages 6 months to 8 years need to receive two doses of the influenza vaccine during their first immunization season, spaced at least 4 weeks apart [9, 10]. Globally, several intervention and survey studies have explored educational strategies to increase influenza vaccination knowledge and attitudes. Abushouk et al. 2023 reported that the targeted educational interventions had a significant effect on the knowledge and practice of health sciences university students regarding the seasonal influenza vaccine in Saudi Arabia [11]. Similarly, Walker et al. (2016) conducted a study amongst medical students in Australia, which found that knowledge and attitudes were strongly linked to vaccination uptake, highlighting the importance of structured learning in improving vaccine uptake [12]. The results of this study suggest that educational programs can be effective in addressing knowledge gaps and vaccine hesitancy across a variety of cultural contexts, supporting the rationale for the current study. To assess the effectiveness of intervention program regarding seasonal influenza vaccine among university students and to enhance vaccination coverage the present study was conducted. 2 Methods Study design: quasi- experimental design was selected to obtain the current study aims. Study period: the study period was 6 months starting from 1st September to the end of February. Data collection was done by working two days per week. The applying of intervention program was continued for 4 months. Study setting: the study was conducted at Thi-qar university, Al- Nasiryiah city, southern Iraq at 6 college out of 18 colleges at the university. The colleges were selected randomly. Study Population: The students of selected colleges of the University were recruited. 17 students from each college were chosen based on a proportional allocation to achieve a total sample of approximately 102 participants per group (17 × 6 = 102), which was determined to be sufficient based on a power analysis (power = 0.80, alpha = 0.05, medium effect size) to detect significant differences in knowledge and attitude scores. 2.1 An intervention group definition The intervention health education program involved four months of structured education through face-to-face lectures (on influenza etiology, transmission, complications and vaccine safety/efficacy); distribution of informational brochures, and interactive question and answer sessions. The intervention group consisted of university students who participated in this education program about seasonal influenza vaccine. 2.2 A control group definition The control group included 102 students (17 students from each of the same 6 colleges) matched to the intervention group by college and academic year that were not went received intervention program on seasonal influenza vaccine. Study Hypothesis: The current study hypothesis display that if there is a significant or non-significant relationship between study variables. - H0: suggest no significant association between pre and post intervention of student knowledge & attitudes regarding seasonal influenza vaccine. - H1: suggest significant association between pre and post intervention of student knowledge & attitudes regarding seasonal influenza vaccine. analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of an educational intervention program on university students’ knowledge and attitudes towards seasonal influenza vaccination in Iraq. Using a quasi-experimental design, 204 students were divided into intervention and control groups, with the intervention group receiving structured educational materials and brochures. Pre- and post-tests were used to measure knowledge and attitudes. Results showed a significant improvement in knowledge, with 55.9% of students achieving high knowledge levels post-intervention compared to 40.2% pre-intervention. Attitudes also shifted, with 73.5% of participants reporting positive attitudes after the intervention, down from 60.8% who had negative attitudes pre-intervention. The authors concluded that the intervention significantly improved knowledge and attitudes (p < 0.001), suggesting that structured educational programs could enhance vaccine acceptance among university students. The study’s findings have implications for public health strategies in Iraq, but the use of a convenience sample and quasi-experimental design may limit generalizability.

papers.title: Recombinant vs Standard Influenza Vaccine in Adults With Severe Obesity: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Individuals with severe obesity are at increased risk of severe influenza and may have impaired immune responses to vaccination. Recombinant influenza vaccine (RIV) may provide enhanced protection compared with egg-based standard-dose influenza vaccine (SD), but data in this high-risk population are limited. METHODS: The AP-HP FLUO trial (NCT05409612) was an open-label, randomized clinical trial conducted in 15 centers in France (November 2022-March 2023) with 6 months of follow-up. Adults with BMI ≥35 kg/m2 were randomized 1:1 to receive RIV or SD, using minimization by center, age (<50 vs ≥50 years), and BMI (<40 vs ≥40 kg/m2). The primary outcome was the ratio (RIV/SD) of geometric mean hemagglutinin-inhibition (HAI) titers (GMTs) for 4 influenza strains 28 days after vaccination. Safety and reactogenicity were also assessed. RESULTS: A total of 206 participants were included (104 RIV, 102 SD). Median age was 50 years, 60.2% were women, and median BMI was 41.0 kg/m2. At Day 28, GMT ratios favored RIV for A/H1N1 (1.6; 95% CI, 1.1-2.3), A/H3N2 (2.0; 95% CI, 1.3-3.2), and B/Yamagata (1.3; 95% CI, 1.0-1.8), but not for B/Victoria (0.9; 95% CI, 0.6-1.3). The effect did not vary significantly across the different age and BMI groups. By Day 180, titers did not differ significantly. Reactogenicity and safety profiles were similar between groups. CONCLUSIONS: In adults with severe obesity, RIV elicited stronger short-term humoral immune responses than an egg-based standard-dose vaccine, suggesting potential additional benefit for influenza prevention in this vulnerable population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Individuals with severe obesity are at increased risk of severe influenza and may have impaired immune responses to vaccination. The study aimed to evaluate the immune response to recombinant influenza vaccine (RIV) versus standard-dose influenza vaccine (SD) in adults with severe obesity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The AP-HP FLUO trial was a randomized clinical trial conducted in 15 centers in France from November 2022 to March 2023, with 6 months of follow-up. Adults with BMI ≥35 kg/m2 were randomized 1:1 to receive RIV or SD, using minimization by center, age (<50 vs ≥50 years), and BMI (<40 vs ≥40 kg/m2).
analysis.methods: The study assessed the geometric mean hemagglutinin-inhibition (HAI) titers for 4 influenza strains 28 days after vaccination. Safety and reactogenicity were also evaluated.
analysis.main_results: A total of 206 participants were included (104 RIV, 102 SD). At Day 28, GMT ratios favored RIV for A/H1N1 (1.6; 95% CI, 1.1-2.3), A/H3N2 (2.0; 95% CI, 1.3-3.2), and B/Yamagata (1.3; 95% CI, 1.0-1.8), but not for B/Victoria (0.9; 95% CI, 0.6-1.3). By Day 180, titers did not differ significantly.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that RIV elicited stronger short-term humoral immune responses than SD in adults with severe obesity, suggesting potential additional benefit for influenza prevention in this population. This finding highlights the immunogenicity of RIV in a vulnerable group.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of vaccination strategies for adults with severe obesity, a high-risk group for influenza complications. They suggest that RIV could offer improved protection in this population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its short follow-up period and the lack of long-term efficacy data. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on a single trial with a relatively small sample size and open-label design.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immune response to recombinant influenza vaccine (RIV) versus standard-dose influenza vaccine (SD) in adults with severe obesity. The AP-HP FLUO trial, conducted in 15 French centers, randomized 206 participants (BMI ≥35 kg/m2) and found that RIV elicited stronger hemagglutinin-inhibition (HAI) titers for A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Yamagata strains at Day 28 compared to SD. However, titers did not differ significantly by Day 180. Reactogenicity and safety profiles were similar between groups. The results suggest that RIV may offer additional benefit for influenza prevention in adults with severe obesity, a vulnerable population. The study's findings are of moderate evidence strength due to its short follow-up and open-label design.
